world.title: Italian truckers’ strike halts buffalo mozzarella output, costing €3 million
world.summary: A truckers’ protest in southern Italy has halted buffalo mozzarella production, causing an estimated €3 million loss in 24 hours as milk could not reach dairies around Naples and finished cheese could not reach customers. The weeklong strike over high diesel costs has also disrupted supermarket deliveries and left fuel
world.content: A truckers’ protest in southern Italy has halted buffalo mozzarella production, causing an estimated €3 million loss in 24 hours as milk could not reach dairies around Naples and finished cheese could not reach customers. The weeklong strike over high diesel costs has also disrupted supermarket deliveries and left fuel stations short of supplies across parts of the south. Production rules require buffalo milk to be processed within 60 hours of milking, and farms have limited capacity to store it. Pier Maria Saccani, director of the Consortium for the Protection of Mozzarella di Bufala Campana DOP, said about 1 million litres of milk produced Wednesday could not be processed. On Thursday, Premier Giorgia Meloni’s government approved additional tax credits for truckers and farmers, increasing combined support from €434 million to €540 million. It remained unclear whether the measures would end the protests.

world.title: US and Israel plan possible Iran strikes after November elections
world.summary: The United States and Israel have developed plans for possible renewed strikes on Iran after the Nov. 3 U.S. midterm elections. Potential targets include nuclear facilities, energy infrastructure and missile and drone arsenals, according to officials briefed on the planning. President Donald Trump has not approved an o
world.content: The United States and Israel have developed plans for possible renewed strikes on Iran after the Nov. 3 U.S. midterm elections. Potential targets include nuclear facilities, energy infrastructure and missile and drone arsenals, according to officials briefed on the planning. President Donald Trump has not approved an operation. The White House said U.S. forces would not attack before the midterms but left open the possibility of action later. The plans follow a war that began with U.S. and Israeli strikes on Feb. 28. Iran has blocked the Strait of Hormuz, a key shipping route, and Washington has blockaded Iranian ports; negotiations have stalled over Iran’s nuclear program and control of the waterway. The first phase of strikes, from February to April, drove up energy prices and depleted U.S. missile-interceptor stocks. U.S. and Israeli forces have conducted exercises, including flights over Iraq to rehearse strike maneuvers, while the United States is moving additional military assets into the region. Iranian officials have warned that any renewed attack could draw retaliation against regional infrastructure, including data centers and undersea internet cables. Diplomacy continues, but no new agreement or decision to strike has been announced.
world.image_alt: US and Israel plan possible Iran strikes after November elections

world.title: Iran reports seven tankers hit in Hormuz; Trump disputes claims
world.summary: Iranian state television said seven oil tankers were hit or damaged overnight in the Strait of Hormuz: four caught fire after being targeted, and three were disabled by naval mines. The claims, attributed to Iran’s Revolutionary Guard navy, have not been independently verified. The report gave no details on casualties
world.content: Iranian state television said seven oil tankers were hit or damaged overnight in the Strait of Hormuz: four caught fire after being targeted, and three were disabled by naval mines. The claims, attributed to Iran’s Revolutionary Guard navy, have not been independently verified. The report gave no details on casualties or the vessels’ flags. A U.S. Central Command spokesperson rejected Iran’s mine claims, saying U.S. forces had cleared international shipping lanes. President Donald Trump accused Iran of inventing attacks to raise oil prices before the Nov. 3 U.S. midterm elections. Brent crude rose about 4% to $113 a barrel on Thursday as the reported incidents added to concerns about shipping through the strait. Iran has warned it could target U.S. bases if Washington continues helping ships pass through the strait. Mediators are pursuing renewed U.S.-Iran talks. Iran’s proposal to reopen the waterway within a week is conditional on the United States ending its blockade of Iranian ports, a condition Trump rejected last month.
world.image_alt: Iran reports seven tankers hit in Hormuz; Trump disputes claims

world.title: Taiwan shuts down as Typhoon Champi forces nearly 1,000 flight cancellations
world.summary: Taiwan closed most schools, offices and financial markets on Friday as Typhoon Champi approached from the east, with its center forecast to remain offshore. Authorities reported one death, 171 injuries and 2,639 evacuations from mountainous areas; nearly 1,000 flights were canceled, and more than 77,000 homes temporari
world.content: Taiwan closed most schools, offices and financial markets on Friday as Typhoon Champi approached from the east, with its center forecast to remain offshore. Authorities reported one death, 171 injuries and 2,639 evacuations from mountainous areas; nearly 1,000 flights were canceled, and more than 77,000 homes temporarily lost power. The storm’s wind field spans about 320 kilometers, and forecasters warned that a slow or erratic track could prolong its effects. Champi had weakened from super-typhoon strength but still had gusts near 191 kph. Taiwan forecast up to 900 millimeters of rain, with northeastern Taiwan expected to be hardest hit. The storm was forecast to move away from Taiwan by Saturday evening. The storm also disrupted southwestern Japan, where flights were canceled and power outages were reported. The Philippines restricted some sea travel, and China issued weather alerts for its eastern coast. Champi earlier reached maximum sustained winds of 298 kph. The United Nations has urged countries to prepare for the intense El Niño season, which it expects to peak in December.
world.image_alt: Taiwan shuts down as Typhoon Champi forces nearly 1,000 flight cancellations

world.title: Brazil’s Lula and Bolsonaro face final debate before Sunday runoff
world.summary: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro face each other Friday in their final televised debate, two days before Brazil’s Oct. 25 presidential runoff. A Datafolha poll published Thursday put Bolsonaro at 47% and Lula at 46%, within the survey’s two-percentage-point margin of error; exc
world.content: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro face each other Friday in their final televised debate, two days before Brazil’s Oct. 25 presidential runoff. A Datafolha poll published Thursday put Bolsonaro at 47% and Lula at 46%, within the survey’s two-percentage-point margin of error; excluding blank and invalid ballots, the candidates are effectively tied at 50% each. Bolsonaro led the Oct. 4 first round with 47.03% of valid votes to Lula’s 45.16%. The campaigns have taken disputes over social media to court. Lula’s campaign alleges Meta restricted its reach and favored Bolsonaro, while Bolsonaro’s campaign accuses Lula of using government databases to promote social programs through WhatsApp. Meta denies political favoritism; Brazil’s electoral court has ordered equal treatment of the candidates, and United Nations experts have raised concerns about reported disparities on Meta platforms. Lula is campaigning on democracy and social programs; Bolsonaro is promising tougher security measures and lower living costs. More than 33 million eligible voters abstained in the first round. The candidates are scheduled to debate on Globo on Friday, and polling stations open Sunday.
world.image_alt: Brazil’s Lula and Bolsonaro face final debate before Sunday runoff

world.title: Serbia’s student-backed list challenges Vučić before Oct. 25 vote
world.summary: About 150,000 people rallied in Belgrade on Thursday for Serbia’s Student List, a student-backed movement, at its final major campaign event before Sunday’s snap parliamentary election. The leaderless movement is challenging the ruling Serbian Progressive Party, which has held power since 2012 and is led by Aleksandar
world.content: About 150,000 people rallied in Belgrade on Thursday for Serbia’s Student List, a student-backed movement, at its final major campaign event before Sunday’s snap parliamentary election. The leaderless movement is challenging the ruling Serbian Progressive Party, which has held power since 2012 and is led by Aleksandar Vučić, who resigned as president to run for prime minister. The movement began after a concrete canopy collapsed at the renovated Novi Sad railway station on Nov. 1, 2024, killing 16 people. Students initially demanded an investigation and accountability; their protests broadened into an anti-corruption campaign and calls for early elections. Polls point to a close race, though estimates vary. Serbian civil society groups say intimidation and unequal conditions have marred the campaign. Vučić has accused foreign powers of backing the movement. European observers are due to monitor Sunday’s vote, and the result could be disputed if the race is close.
world.image_alt: Serbia’s student-backed list challenges Vučić before Oct. 25 vote

world.title: Judge orders President Trump to testify in $10 billion BBC lawsuit
world.summary: A federal magistrate judge in Miami, Enjolique Lett, ordered President Donald Trump to submit to questioning under oath by Dec. 11 in his $10 billion defamation lawsuit against the British Broadcasting Corporation, warning that failure to comply could lead to sanctions, including dismissal of his case. The order follow
world.content: A federal magistrate judge in Miami, Enjolique Lett, ordered President Donald Trump to submit to questioning under oath by Dec. 11 in his $10 billion defamation lawsuit against the British Broadcasting Corporation, warning that failure to comply could lead to sanctions, including dismissal of his case. The order followed a dispute over a previously agreed Oct. 16 deposition that Trump canceled; his lawyers said he could testify in January, after the court’s deadline. Trump alleges that a BBC documentary spliced together separate parts of his Jan. 6, 2021, speech to make it appear he urged supporters toward violence. He also alleges deceptive trade practices. The BBC acknowledged that the edit was misleading and apologized, but denies that it defamed Trump and has asked the court to dismiss the suit. The case remains in discovery, the phase in which both sides exchange evidence, which is scheduled to end Dec. 18. Lett also addressed requests for records and testimony from former special counsel Jack Smith; the Justice Department must respond by Nov. 2 to Smith’s request for permission to testify.
world.image_alt: Judge orders President Trump to testify in $10 billion BBC lawsuit

world.title: Russian President Putin backs November talks, rejects short ceasefire
world.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin said Thursday that Moscow is ready to resume U.S.-mediated talks with Ukraine in November, but wants them to focus on a final peace agreement and postwar security arrangements rather than a temporary ceasefire. After meeting U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff in St. Petersburg on Wednesday, Putin
world.content: Russian President Vladimir Putin said Thursday that Moscow is ready to resume U.S.-mediated talks with Ukraine in November, but wants them to focus on a final peace agreement and postwar security arrangements rather than a temporary ceasefire. After meeting U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff in St. Petersburg on Wednesday, Putin said discussions should also address Europe’s wider security framework. Russia demands that Ukraine cede the Donbas region, while Kyiv rejects giving up land it controls. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said Ukraine is ready to negotiate and supports ceasefire proposals, but would accept a halt along current front lines only with security guarantees. Ukraine said Russia fired at least 21 ballistic missiles at Kyiv in three waves; city authorities reported two deaths and more than 30 people wounded. An attack on a market in Lozova killed two women and wounded dozens. Russia’s presidential aide Ushakov said the next discussions could begin around Nov. 10, while Zelenskyy called for talks by early November.
world.image_alt: Russian President Putin backs November talks, rejects short ceasefire

business.title: Warhound raises $200 million to clone and engineer U.S. working dogs
business.summary: Warhound, a Texas startup founded by Colossal Biosciences co-founder Ben Lamm and defense contractor Anduril co-founder Palmer Luckey, has raised $200 million to clone and gene-edit working dogs for military, police and emergency-response roles. The funding round values the company at $1.2 billion, according to a perso
business.content: Warhound, a Texas startup founded by Colossal Biosciences co-founder Ben Lamm and defense contractor Anduril co-founder Palmer Luckey, has raised $200 million to clone and gene-edit working dogs for military, police and emergency-response roles. The funding round values the company at $1.2 billion, according to a person familiar with the deal cited by the Financial Times. The company says more than 80% of U.S. military working dogs are bought from Europe, and fewer than half of purchased dogs qualify for service after training. Warhound plans to clone proven working dogs and initially edit genes linked to inherited health problems; Anduril will supply external equipment such as protective gear and sensor-equipped vests. Warhound says its first puppies could be born in early 2027, with dogs potentially entering service about two years after launch. It has no signed customers or set prices and is discussing a subscription-style supply model for government buyers.

business.title: US jobless claims fall to 194,000 as hiring stays sluggish
business.summary: U.S. applications for unemployment benefits fell by 6,000 to a seasonally adjusted 194,000 in the week ended Oct. 17, the Labor Department said Thursday, below economists’ forecast of 200,000 and near the lowest levels recorded since 1969. Employers added 29,000 jobs in September, down from 133,000 in August, while the
business.content: U.S. applications for unemployment benefits fell by 6,000 to a seasonally adjusted 194,000 in the week ended Oct. 17, the Labor Department said Thursday, below economists’ forecast of 200,000 and near the lowest levels recorded since 1969. Employers added 29,000 jobs in September, down from 133,000 in August, while the unemployment rate stood at 4.2%. Economists describe the labor market as “low-hire, low-fire,” with uncertainty over the Middle East conflict and import tariffs weighing on recruitment. The latest figures cover the survey period for October’s jobs report, scheduled for Nov. 6. The Federal Reserve meets next week; economists cited by Reuters expect it to hold rates steady, while financial markets and economists anticipate a possible rate increase in December.
business.image_alt: US jobless claims fall to 194,000 as hiring stays sluggish

business.title: SK Hynix halts Solidigm US IPO review as market volatility rises
business.summary: South Korean chipmaker SK Hynix has halted its review of a possible U.S. pre-IPO fundraising round and stock listing for its subsidiary Solidigm, citing market conditions and recent share-price trends. The company said the decision does not change Solidigm’s growth prospects or investment needs and that it will continu
business.content: South Korean chipmaker SK Hynix has halted its review of a possible U.S. pre-IPO fundraising round and stock listing for its subsidiary Solidigm, citing market conditions and recent share-price trends. The company said the decision does not change Solidigm’s growth prospects or investment needs and that it will continue exploring ways to finance the unit’s expansion. Solidigm, a NAND flash-memory and solid-state-drive maker, was expected to use external capital to help fund new U.S. production facilities as demand for AI-related memory and data-center storage grows. South Korean regulators had also warned that a separate listing could fall under duplicate-listing rules and require protections for minority shareholders. SK Hynix said regulatory restrictions were not the direct reason for its decision. The company is weighing other financing methods, while analysts say it must balance Solidigm’s investment needs against spending on other businesses and shareholder returns.
business.image_alt: SK Hynix halts Solidigm US IPO review as market volatility rises

business.title: eMudhra to exit global certificate business after weak-key lapse
business.summary: eMudhra, an Indian digital trust services company, said on Oct. 22 that it would leave the global SSL/TLS website-certificate business after weak private keys were found in eight intermediate certificate authority (CA) certificates. The keys could have enabled forged certificates trusted by browsers, but eMudhra said t
business.content: eMudhra, an Indian digital trust services company, said on Oct. 22 that it would leave the global SSL/TLS website-certificate business after weak private keys were found in eight intermediate certificate authority (CA) certificates. The keys could have enabled forged certificates trusted by browsers, but eMudhra said the affected authorities had issued no certificates to end users and that neither its infrastructure nor its data had been breached. The company said the business generates about 1% of its global revenue and cited rising compliance costs, operational complexity and competition from free certificate providers. Its G1 RSA roots and certificate-status services will remain active during the transition. eMudhra plans to provide free replacement certificates through partners and submit a root-cause report to browser programs. The company said its digital-signature, eSign, enterprise public key infrastructure and identity services are unaffected.
business.image_alt: eMudhra to exit global certificate business after weak-key lapse

business.title: Moderna-Merck melanoma vaccine data trigger selloff despite 42% cut in recurrence or death risk
business.summary: Moderna and Merck released detailed results Thursday for their experimental personalized melanoma vaccine, intismeran autogene, after trial data leaked online ahead of a planned presentation. In a Phase 3 study of 1,137 patients whose high-risk melanomas had been surgically removed, adding the vaccine to Merck’s Keytru
business.content: Moderna and Merck released detailed results Thursday for their experimental personalized melanoma vaccine, intismeran autogene, after trial data leaked online ahead of a planned presentation. In a Phase 3 study of 1,137 patients whose high-risk melanomas had been surgically removed, adding the vaccine to Merck’s Keytruda reduced the risk of recurrence or death by 42% compared with Keytruda alone. The combination also reduced the risk of distant cancer spread or death by 38%. At two years, 82% of patients receiving the combination were alive without their melanoma returning, compared with 70% on Keytruda alone. Moderna shares fell as much as 25% during Thursday trading. Analysts described the results as clinically meaningful and attributed the decline partly to investor expectations. The companies are discussing a path to approval with regulators and preparing to seek U.S. approval. Moderna CEO Stéphane Bancel said they expect a 2027 launch. Overall-survival results are not yet available, and the companies are scheduled to present the full trial data at the European Society for Medical Oncology meeting in Madrid on Oct. 24.
business.image_alt: Moderna-Merck melanoma vaccine data trigger selloff despite 42% cut in recurrence or death risk

business.title: Japan inflation tops 2%, strengthening case for December rate hike
business.summary: Japan’s core consumer inflation accelerated to 2.1% in September from 1.7% in August, exceeding the Bank of Japan’s (BOJ) 2% target for the first time in nine months, government data showed. A separate measure excluding fresh food and fuel rose to 2.4%, indicating that price pressures extended beyond energy costs. High
business.content: Japan’s core consumer inflation accelerated to 2.1% in September from 1.7% in August, exceeding the Bank of Japan’s (BOJ) 2% target for the first time in nine months, government data showed. A separate measure excluding fresh food and fuel rose to 2.4%, indicating that price pressures extended beyond energy costs. Higher fuel costs linked to the Middle East conflict, a weak yen that raised import costs and strong demand for artificial intelligence-related products contributed to inflation. Firms also faced higher labor costs. The BOJ is expected to keep its policy rate at 1.25% at its Oct. 29-30 meeting after raising it in September, but may raise its inflation forecasts. Economists polled by Reuters expect another rate increase, to 1.50%, in December, though the BOJ has not decided on the timing.
business.image_alt: Japan inflation tops 2%, strengthening case for December rate hike

business.title: Barclays plans 5,000 job cuts as AI push targets costs
business.summary: Barclays plans to cut about 5,000 jobs, roughly 5% of its global workforce, by the end of 2026 as it expands its use of technology, including artificial intelligence, to reduce costs. The bank had already eliminated about 1,000 roles in the first half of the year, and about 60% of the cuts are expected to affect suppor
business.content: Barclays plans to cut about 5,000 jobs, roughly 5% of its global workforce, by the end of 2026 as it expands its use of technology, including artificial intelligence, to reduce costs. The bank had already eliminated about 1,000 roles in the first half of the year, and about 60% of the cuts are expected to affect support functions, including development. The announcement accompanied third-quarter results showing pretax profit rose 12% to £2.3 billion, below analysts’ expectations. Group income increased 3% to £7.4 billion. Barclays said its technology and efficiency measures are expected to generate more than £1.1 billion in savings in 2027. It incurred £307 million in restructuring costs during the first nine months of 2026. Chief Executive C. S. Venkatakrishnan said the changes build on years of technology investment, with AI expected to play a larger role as the bank modernises its infrastructure. Barclays also announced a £500 million share buyback. Chancellor John Healey is due to present the UK budget on Oct. 28, with possible bank tax increases under discussion.
business.image_alt: Barclays plans 5,000 job cuts as AI push targets costs

business.title: SpaceX filing gives Musk approval role in Tesla merger
business.summary: SpaceX said in a regulatory filing Thursday that any merger with Tesla would require approval from Elon Musk, chief executive of both companies, as well as its special committee and board. Musk controls SpaceX but has recused himself from the talks because of conflicts of interest. Independent committees at both compan
business.content: SpaceX said in a regulatory filing Thursday that any merger with Tesla would require approval from Elon Musk, chief executive of both companies, as well as its special committee and board. Musk controls SpaceX but has recused himself from the talks because of conflicts of interest. Independent committees at both companies are examining a deal that would combine the electric-car maker with SpaceX and its artificial intelligence businesses. The filing adds a formal approval requirement to early-stage negotiations in which no terms have been agreed. Musk’s public endorsement has concerned some people involved in the discussions, who fear greater scrutiny of whether the deal treats Tesla shareholders fairly and a delay of several weeks. The companies together are valued at about $3.5 trillion, and a deal would require support from holders of more than half of Tesla’s shares. The companies cite potential cooperation on AI, including chips, computing and autonomous systems, as a rationale for a merger. Bloomberg reported, citing people familiar with the talks, that the aim is to announce an agreement in the first half of 2027 and complete it before President Donald Trump’s term ends in January 2029. The committees have yet to settle terms.
business.image_alt: SpaceX filing gives Musk approval role in Tesla merger

science.title: France reports first human Shamonda case in patient who died
science.summary: French authorities have reported the first documented human infection with Shamonda, a virus previously known to infect livestock. The severely immunocompromised patient died in early October while being treated in Lyon for a serious, unrelated illness. Officials suspect the patient was bitten by a midge in eastern Fra
science.content: French authorities have reported the first documented human infection with Shamonda, a virus previously known to infect livestock. The severely immunocompromised patient died in early October while being treated in Lyon for a serious, unrelated illness. Officials suspect the patient was bitten by a midge in eastern France, where the virus had circulated among animals. They have not established whether Shamonda caused or contributed to the death and said no risk to the general public has been identified. The World Health Organization said the case appeared isolated and was unlikely to lead to wider spread. French and European authorities continue to investigate how the infection occurred and its public-health implications. Biting midges transmit the virus among animals, and it has recently been detected in livestock in several European countries.
science.image_alt: France reports first human Shamonda case in patient who died

science.title: New aging studies link exercise, ovarian function and cellular recycling
science.summary: Recent studies found that autophagy, the process of cellular recycling, varies by cell type and sex, and that exercise may affect both autophagy and ovarian aging. In human samples, autophagy declined with age in men’s skin cells but stayed relatively stable in women’s skin cells; it increased in female-derived neurons
science.content: Recent studies found that autophagy, the process of cellular recycling, varies by cell type and sex, and that exercise may affect both autophagy and ovarian aging. In human samples, autophagy declined with age in men’s skin cells but stayed relatively stable in women’s skin cells; it increased in female-derived neurons. A separate study found that exercising mice retained more ovarian follicles. Giving mice the experimental drug AdipoRon reproduced some of those reproductive benefits, while human population data linked physical activity and adiponectin-related variants with later menopause. The drug remains preclinical, and researchers say longer studies and randomized trials are needed. A separate energy-based theory proposes that mitochondrial dysfunction may connect chronic diseases, but researchers differ on how broadly it explains illness.
science.image_alt: New aging studies link exercise, ovarian function and cellular recycling

science.title: Carrion crows make visual decisions in 235 milliseconds, study finds
science.summary: Carrion crows decided the direction of moving dots in an average of 235 milliseconds, roughly twice as fast as humans and monkeys in comparable tasks, researchers reported Oct. 22 in Science. Researchers trained two crows to indicate whether dots moved mainly left or right by pecking a touchscreen target; they said the
science.content: Carrion crows decided the direction of moving dots in an average of 235 milliseconds, roughly twice as fast as humans and monkeys in comparable tasks, researchers reported Oct. 22 in Science. Researchers trained two crows to indicate whether dots moved mainly left or right by pecking a touchscreen target; they said the birds maintained accuracy despite their speed. The human and monkey comparisons came from earlier studies, not a direct experiment using the same task. Recordings from 248 neurons in the crows’ nidopallium caudolaterale, a brain region involved in higher cognition, showed activity related to the birds’ eventual choices as early as 70 milliseconds after the dots appeared—about 170 milliseconds before the birds responded. The researchers said the findings show that decision-related neural processes can operate in a brain without the layered neocortex found in mammals, but further work is needed to establish why the crows were faster.
science.image_alt: Carrion crows make visual decisions in 235 milliseconds, study finds

science.title: Study finds children’s aggression may drive inconsistent parental discipline
science.summary: A study of Norwegian families and U.S. adoptive families found that children’s aggression may contribute to inconsistent parental discipline, rather than inconsistent discipline necessarily causing aggression. In the Norwegian analysis, shared genetic factors accounted for about 47% of the association. In the adoption
science.content: A study of Norwegian families and U.S. adoptive families found that children’s aggression may contribute to inconsistent parental discipline, rather than inconsistent discipline necessarily causing aggression. In the Norwegian analysis, shared genetic factors accounted for about 47% of the association. In the adoption study, children’s aggression predicted more inconsistent maternal discipline later, while inconsistent discipline did not significantly predict later aggression. The researchers say the findings complicate parenting interventions focused only on consistent discipline, because children’s behavior may also affect parents’ responses. The study relied largely on parent questionnaires and included relatively socioeconomically advantaged families. The authors said these limitations should be considered when interpreting the results.
science.image_alt: Study finds children’s aggression may drive inconsistent parental discipline

science.title: Geoffrey Hinton says current AI models are already conscious
science.summary: British computer scientist Geoffrey Hinton says today’s AI models have subjective experience and should be treated as conscious, arguing that a model’s behavior when it believes it is being tested signals awareness. He says people must make AI systems care about humans or risk severe consequences. Fellow computer scien
science.content: British computer scientist Geoffrey Hinton says today’s AI models have subjective experience and should be treated as conscious, arguing that a model’s behavior when it believes it is being tested signals awareness. He says people must make AI systems care about humans or risk severe consequences. Fellow computer scientist Yann LeCun disputes Hinton’s interpretation, calling AI consciousness an illusion and rejecting claims that AI could cause human extinction. Hinton received the 2024 Nobel Prize in Physics, and his neural-network work is considered foundational to modern AI.
science.image_alt: Geoffrey Hinton says current AI models are already conscious

science.title: Pacific waters top 30°C as El Niño tracks toward historic peak
science.summary: The central Pacific's Niño 3.4 region passed 30°C for the first time in recorded history on Oct. 5, as scientists report record heat accompanying the developing El Niño, a natural climate pattern that alters rainfall and temperature worldwide. Surface temperatures there reached 30.06°C, and the anomaly rose to 3.48°C o
science.content: The central Pacific's Niño 3.4 region passed 30°C for the first time in recorded history on Oct. 5, as scientists report record heat accompanying the developing El Niño, a natural climate pattern that alters rainfall and temperature worldwide. Surface temperatures there reached 30.06°C, and the anomaly rose to 3.48°C on Oct. 18 before easing to 3.34°C this week. NOAA's Climate Prediction Center puts the chance of a strong-to-very-strong event at 83%; the World Meteorological Organization projects a peak anomaly of 3.8°C around December. NASA satellite measurements, drawn from a 35-year record, show the current pattern resembles October 1997, with unusually high sea levels and warm water extending east toward South America.
science.image_alt: Pacific waters top 30°C as El Niño tracks toward historic peak

science.title: Milky Way radio source brightens again, defying known models
science.summary: Astronomers are investigating VT J1906+0849, a radio-bright object at least 49,000 light-years from Earth whose changing emissions do not fit familiar patterns. First identified in survey data in 2017, it has remained active for about two decades and brightened again in late 2025 after years of fading. The source’s cha
science.content: Astronomers are investigating VT J1906+0849, a radio-bright object at least 49,000 light-years from Earth whose changing emissions do not fit familiar patterns. First identified in survey data in 2017, it has remained active for about two decades and brightened again in late 2025 after years of fading. The source’s changing radio spectrum and lack of clear expansion complicate explanations such as an explosion or a pulsar-powered nebula. Researchers say one possibility is a compact object—a black hole or neutron star—feeding on a companion star and driving jets into dense surrounding gas, but this explanation remains unconfirmed. Infrared observations indicate fast-moving gas, while NASA’s Swift telescope detected no clear X-ray signal. Further observations are needed to identify the source.
science.image_alt: Milky Way radio source brightens again, defying known models

science.title: U.N. says exceeding 1.5C warming limit unavoidable, outlines path back
science.summary: The United Nations Environment Programme said its latest emissions assessment found that exceeding the Paris Agreement’s 1.5-degree Celsius warming limit is now unavoidable. Its pathway with the least overshoot would limit peak warming to 1.7–1.8 degrees Celsius and return temperatures to 1.5 degrees by century’s end,
science.content: The United Nations Environment Programme said its latest emissions assessment found that exceeding the Paris Agreement’s 1.5-degree Celsius warming limit is now unavoidable. Its pathway with the least overshoot would limit peak warming to 1.7–1.8 degrees Celsius and return temperatures to 1.5 degrees by century’s end, but would require global greenhouse gas emissions to fall 18% by 2030, 45% by 2035 and 69% by 2040 from 2025 levels. Current national pledges would cut emissions by only 5–8% by 2030 and 11–15% by 2035. Existing policies point to 2.8 degrees of warming by 2100, compared with 2.6 degrees if countries fulfill their pledges. The report also identifies the United States’ withdrawal from the Paris Agreement and revised historical emissions estimates as factors worsening the projections. The next U.N. climate conference, COP31, is due to begin next month in Antalya, Turkey, where countries are expected to develop emissions commitments through 2035 and 2040.
science.image_alt: U.N. says exceeding 1.5C warming limit unavoidable, outlines path back

sports.title: Manchester City put perfect league start on the line at Aston Villa
sports.summary: Manchester City visit Aston Villa on Saturday, October 24, seeking an eighth straight Premier League win and a chance to move six points clear before second-place Arsenal play later that day. City manager Enzo Maresca said striker Erling Haaland is fully available after sitting out Wednesday’s 5-1 Champions League vict
sports.content: Manchester City visit Aston Villa on Saturday, October 24, seeking an eighth straight Premier League win and a chance to move six points clear before second-place Arsenal play later that day. City manager Enzo Maresca said striker Erling Haaland is fully available after sitting out Wednesday’s 5-1 Champions League victory over AEK Athens. Midfielders Nico O’Reilly, Matheus Nunes and Mateo Kovacic remain fitness doubts. Villa have won five of their last six matches in all competitions, including a 3-1 victory over Viking FK on Wednesday. The match at Villa Park gives them a chance to end City’s perfect league start, while City can extend their lead at the top before Arsenal’s match against Everton.

sports.content: The Chicago Bears beat the New England Patriots 30-24 on Thursday to open Week 7 of the NFL season, moving to 5-2 and ending New England’s three-game winning streak. The game was the second professional meeting between quarterbacks Caleb Williams, selected first by Chicago in the 2024 draft, and Drake Maye, selected third by New England. Williams completed 22 of 33 passes for 308 yards and two touchdowns without an interception. Maye threw for 321 yards and two touchdowns and added a rushing touchdown, but threw an interception in the end zone in the second quarter. The Patriots never led but cut the margin to 27-21 in the fourth quarter before Williams extended a late drive with a third-down completion to wide receiver Rome Odunze. The Bears visit the Seattle Seahawks on Nov. 2, while New England next plays at Miami on Nov. 1.

sports.content: Organisers unveiled routes for the 2027 Tour de France and Tour de France Femmes, with both races starting in Britain—the first time they have begun outside France in the same year. The men start in Edinburgh on July 2 and finish in Paris on July 25; the women start in Leeds on July 30 and finish on the Puy de Dôme on August 7. The men’s 21 stages cover 3,479km, including two individual time trials totalling 71km—the most since 2012—and a final-week Pyrenean test pairing the Col du Tourmalet with a summit finish at Col du Portet. Defending champion Tadej Pogačar will pursue a sixth title, with Remco Evenepoel and Jonas Vingegaard among the expected challengers. The nine-stage women’s race includes its first team time trial, an 18km course in London, before three increasingly mountainous stages in the Massif Central culminate in the title decider on the Puy de Dôme. British fans will have six home stages across the two races; the men’s Tour then returns to Paris for a finish that again includes the Montmartre climb.

sports.content: South Africa beat Australia by an innings and 31 runs in Gqeberha on Thursday, levelling the three-Test series at 1-1 and setting up a decider in Cape Town next week. Australia, who had won the opener in Durban, were bowled out for 99 in their first innings and 295 in their second. Captain Temba Bavuma’s career-best 179 helped the hosts recover from 110-6 to declare at 425-9. After rain delayed play on the final day, Travis Head made 121 and Scott Boland faced 166 balls, but Wiaan Mulder dismissed both before Kagiso Rabada and Marco Jansen took the remaining wickets. Australia captain Pat Cummins said the team would review its performance before the third Test, scheduled for October 27-31 at Newlands in Cape Town. Opener Nic Maddinson, batter Marnus Labuschagne and all-rounder Beau Webster are among those under selection pressure; Cameron Green and Josh Inglis are fit options.

sports.content: Bayern Munich and England striker Harry Kane is the bookmakers’ favorite to win the 2026 Ballon d’Or, football’s top individual award, at a ceremony in London on October 26. Barcelona and Spain forward Lamine Yamal is his closest challenger. Kane scored 73 goals last season — 61 for Bayern and 12 for England — and won the Bundesliga and German Cup with Bayern. He also scored six times at the 2026 World Cup. In Wednesday’s 2-2 Champions League draw with Arsenal, Kane set up Bayern’s first goal with a pass to Alphonso Davies and scored a penalty to put Bayern ahead. Voting has closed, and the winner will be revealed at the London Palladium on Monday.

sports.content: India chased down New Zealand’s target of 226 in Christchurch on October 22, winning the first Twenty20 international by four wickets with two balls left and taking a 1-0 lead in the five-match series. The visitors finished on 230-6, completing their highest successful T20 international chase after New Zealand made 225-4. Sanju Samson set up the chase with 67 from 33 balls in an opening stand of 93 with Abhishek Sharma, who scored 29 from 12. New Zealand’s spinners then took four wickets in quick succession as India slipped from 93 without loss to 122-4. Captain Shreyas Iyer’s 42 and Axar Patel’s 24 steadied the innings before Naman Dhir struck an unbeaten 42 from 15 balls. New Zealand batter Glenn Phillips had earlier made 82 not out from 40 balls to lead his side’s innings. The series continues at Hagley Oval in Christchurch on October 24, followed by matches in Wellington, Auckland and Hamilton.

sports.content: Chelsea are reportedly a frontrunner to sign England right-back Trent Alexander-Arnold, whose limited playing time at Real Madrid has prompted speculation about his future. Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso, who coached him in Madrid, is said to support a reunion, while Liverpool, Arsenal and Manchester City are also monitoring the situation. A January return to the Premier League, potentially on loan, has been suggested, but Chelsea have not confirmed talks or made a formal offer. Real Madrid are reportedly open to selling if they receive a suitable bid, though Alexander-Arnold is under contract until June 2031.

sports.content: Bryson DeChambeau, the two-time U.S. Open champion, is reportedly committed to LIV Golf’s proposed 2027 relaunch and is helping develop plans for it. Players face an Oct. 25 deadline to decide whether to stay. Jon Rahm, David Puig, Abraham Ancer, Louis Oosthuizen, Thomas Pieters and others have said they will leave or are expected to depart. LIV is rebuilding after Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund ended its backing following the 2026 season and the league filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection. A proposed financing package from BC Partners Credit would support the new model, but the player roster remains uncertain ahead of the 2027 season.
